# Explain Skills and Progressive Disclosure in an Agent

[← AMD](../README.md) · [Every AMD question](../../amd.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/explain-skills-and-progressive-disclosure-in-an-agent)

---

Describe the concept of a skill within an agent architecture, contrast it with a standard prompt, and discuss how progressive disclosure can structure the information provided to the agent.
### Constraints & Assumptions
Assume a generic architecture: a skill is a reusable task bundle that includes instructions and may also contain references or tools. Do not rely on any particular product's file format or loading mechanism.
### Clarifying Questions
How are skills discovered and chosen? What information is loaded at the start? Who is responsible for permissions and validation? What occurs if a referenced document is untrusted or out of date?
### What a Strong Answer Covers
Reusable procedures compared to per-interaction instructions, staged loading, tradeoffs in context and selection, and the boundaries of what a skill can guarantee.
### Follow-up Questions
How can an excess of skill descriptions impair selection? At what point should detailed references be loaded? Why does bundling a procedure not grant authority to every instruction in a retrieved document?
Overview:
Explain reusable agent skills, prompt context, progressive disclosure, selection metadata, referenced resources, and the limits of permissions and validation.
